interface.shortDescription: Shared file-based memory for Codex and Claude Code.
interface.longDescription: Release v0.37.0 adds optional source-bound memory revocation across supported recall, memory units, procedures, ledger assembly, SessionStart context, link proposals and new OKF exports. Only explicitly selected physical line spans and declared derivations are masked; unrelated lines and original source/hash/line identity are preserved. This is not semantic-equivalence inference, undeclared-copy discovery or erasure of Git history, backups or old external exports. Malformed, stale or unsafe configured bindings fail closed; absent configuration preserves existing defaults. An offline deterministic lifecycle evaluator runs real store, correction, replay and relearning operations in fresh Python processes; synthetic controls are not LLM robustness scores. The shared webapp-principles skill and six-rule guide, explicit dependency impact review, limited selected-note OKF exchange and earlier opt-in diagnostics remain available. Native discovery verifies both enabled skills and exact required bundled resource bytes, not application compliance. The seven certificate-bound checker files and harmless corpus remain compatible with v0.36.1 when actually installed bound bytes match. For older transitions where checker_sha256 changes: if warnings were promoted to fatal, revert them to warning, bring the Claude Code and Codex installations and a git vault's 00-meta/scripts engine copy to the same version (also when rolling back), regenerate the certificate there, then promote again. Regeneration includes the harmless replay. Publication does not authorize active installation changes or company-vault activation. No default model/network call or runtime dependency is added.
